out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: OBSERVED RAW SHELL EGGS IN THE WALK IN COOLER STORED ABOVE READY TO EAT FOOD
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CFM MOVED THE RAW SHELL EGGS FROM ABOVE THE READY TO EAT FOOD.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: COOKED BEANS STORED IN A LARGE, COVERED, PLASTIC CONTAINER IN THE WALK IN COOLER WERE 50F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. KITCHEN STAFF MEMBER DISCARDED THE PRODUCT.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure: CARNE ASADA AND SALMON ARE UNDERCOOKED PER CUSTOMER REQUEST; HOWEVER, THERE IS NOT AN ASTERISK LINKING THE FOODS TO THE CONSUMER ADVISORY REMINDER.
violations.corrective_action: The Consumer Advisory shall include a disclosure statement that includes a description of the animal-derived foods as raw/undercooked or identification of the animal-derived foods by asterisking (*) them to a footnote that states that the items are served raw or undercooked, or contain raw or undercooked ingredients. THE FACILITY MUST PROVIDE A CONSUMER ADVISORY DISCLOSURE (ASTERISK) FOR ALL RAW OR UNDERCOOK PROTEINS. ALTERNATIVELY, THE CARNE ASADA AND SALMON MUST BE SERVED FULLY COOKED TO ALL CUSTOMERS. CORRECT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: COOKED BEANS IN THE WALK IN COOLER OBSERVED IN A LARGE, COVERED PLASTIC CONTAINER. THE PRODUCT WAS LABELED AS BEING PREPARED THE DAY BEFORE AT APPROXIMATELY 5:30P. THE PRODUCT WAS 50F.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. THE PRODUCT WAS DISCARDED BY THE KITCHEN STAFF. CFM AND EHS DISCUSSED THE METHODS USED TO COOL FOODS WITHIN THE ESTABLISHMENT, AND BEFORE THE PRODUCT IS COMBINED AND COVERED, IT MUST BE 41F OR LESS. USE ICE BATHS AND ICE WANDS TO AID IN COOLING. STIR FREQUENTLY TO RELEASE HEAT.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Pest Control Methods
violations.observation: Methods are not being used to control pests. OBSERVED LIVE COCKROACH IN THE KITCHEN ON THE BACKSPLASH OF THE COOK LINE AND ON THE WALL OF THE TORTILLA CHIP SERVING STATION.
violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. If pests are found on the premises methods shall be used to control their presence. CFM STATED A LICENSED PEST CONTROL COMPANY HAD BEEN TO THE FACILITY ON OCTOBER 15 AND 20 TO TREAT FOR PESTS. PROVIDE EHS WITH TREATMENT INVOICE FROM THE OCTOBER 20TH SERVICE TO VERIFY SERVICE. IF THERE IS AN INCREASE IN PEST ACTIVITY, CONTACT YOUR PEST CONTROL COMPANY FOR ADDITIONAL SERVICE/PRESCRIPTIONS. MORE FREQUENT AND THOROUGH CLEANING IS REQUIRED IN ADDITION TO REPAIRING DEFECTS IN THE KITCHEN WALLS. FOLLOW UP WILL BE CONDUCTED WITHIN 10 DAYS.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: OBSERVED A BUILD UP OF GREASE AND FOOD DEBRIS ON THE FLOOR AND BACKSPLASH IN THE KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. FLOORS AND WALLS SHOULD BE CLEANED TO SIGHT AND TOUCH. CORRECT THE VIOLATION PRIOR TO THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Floors/Walls/Ceilings, Materials Smooth, Durable, Cleanable
violations.observation: OBSERVED METAL FLASHING AFFIXED TO THE WALLS IN THE KITCHEN ALONG THE COOK LINE NOT SEALED TO THE WALL. THE AREA BEHIND THE FLASHING IS NOT EASILY CLEANABLE.
violations.corrective_action: Wall, floor, and ceiling surfaces shall be smooth, durable, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent for areas subject to moisture such as food preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, warewashing areas, and toilet rooms. THE WALLS IN THE KITCHEN SHOULD BE SMOOTH, DURABLE AND EASILY CLEANABLE. THE FLASHING SHOULD BE SEALED TO THE WALLS OR REMOVED. CORRECT THE VIOLATION BEFORE THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.observation: Observed cutting boards heavily scored throughout the kitchen
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces such as cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC TO REPLACE CUTTING BOARDS AS THEY ARE HARDER TO SANITIZE.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed an unapproved backflow prevention device attached to the mop sink.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. EHS PROVIDED PIC WITH INFORMATION ABOUT AN APPROVED BACKFLOW PREVENTION DEVICE. ORDER AND INSTALL.

violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. EHS PROVIDED PIC WITH A HANDWASHING SIGN TO POST.

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: Observed staff not washing their hands after changing gloves.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. PIC INSTRUCTED STAFF MEMBER TO REMOVE GLOVES AND WASH HANDS BEFORE PUTTING ON NEW GLOVES. HAND WASHING MUST OCCUR AFTER CHANGING TASKS AND BEFORE PUTTING NEW GLOVES ON, ESPECIALLY WHEN HANDLING RAW PROTEINS AND ALLERGENS. SEE WHEN TO WASH HANDOUT/FACT SHEET.

violations.observation: Observed staff with gloved hands touch cooked chicken and raw shrimp without changing gloves.
violations.corrective_action: If used, single-use gloves shall be used for only ONE task and used for no other purposes. The single-use gloves shall be discarded when damaged or soiled or when interruptions occur in the operation. PIC INSTRUCTED STAFF TO CHANGE GLOVES IN BETWEEN HANDLING COOKED FOODS AND RAW FOODS TO AVOID CROSS CONTAMINATION. SEE GLOVES USE HANDOUT/FACT SHEET. UNCLE JULIO'S RIO GRANDE CAFE (Inspection Date: 03/20/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: EH observed salsa being held on time outside of a coldwell or ice with no written 4 hr end point
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. PIC wrote end points on salsa containers

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Wash Temp for Hot Water Warewashing Machines
violations.observation: The wash water temperature of the hot water sanitizing warewashing machine is not meeting the manufacturer's specifications. The minimum temperature was 160 while the actual temperature was 135
violations.corrective_action: The temperature of the wash solution in spray type warewashers that use hot water to sanitize may not be less than: 1) 165F for a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 2) 150F for a stationary rack, dual temperature machine, 3) 160F for a single tank, conveyor, dual temperature machine, or 4) 150F for a multitank, conveyor, multitemperature machine. PIC Had Dishmachine company repair man fix machine during inspection
